message.reasoning_content:
The image shows a Rolex Cosmograph Daytona with a black dial, silver/steel subdials (actually the subdials appear light/silver with black rings), black ceramic bezel with tachymeter. This appears to be the "Daytona" 116500LN with black dial and steel bezel... wait, 116500LN has a ceramic bezel. The reference with black dial and silver subdials...

Black dial Daytona with steel Oyster bracelet and ceramic bezel: 116500LN black dial. Actually the black dial 116500LN has silver subdials. Yes, 116500LN-0002 is black dial.

Wait — the subdials here look light gray/silver with black outer rings. Yes that matches 116500LN black dial. Hmm, but actually the subdials on the black dial 116500LN are silver with... yes.

Actually, note the hands: the central hands appear gold-ish? The hour/minute hands on 116500LN are... The 116500LN has steel hands with lume. The image hands look pale/gold-ish which could be lighting.

Alternatively this could be 116520 black dial (steel bezel) — no, the bezel here is ceramic black with tachymeter numerals in white — that's the ceramic bezel 116500LN.

So reference: 116500LN (black dial). Confidence ~0.75.

Movement: automatic (Caliber 4130). Case material: stainless steel. Bracelet: metal (Oystersteel).

Model family: Cosmograph Daytona.

Reference number format: 116500LN. Some write "116500LN-0002" but the brand's official is 116500LN. I'll give 116500LN.

Confidence maybe 0.7.
